Query: What is the tax year for income tax purposes?
Answer: The 'tax year' refers to the twelve-month period of the financial year commencing on the 1st of April, or in the case of a newly set up business or source of income, the period beginning from the date of setting up or commencement and ending with the said financial year.

Query: How do I know if I am a resident of India for tax reasons?
Answer: An individual is deemed to be resident in India in a tax year if such individual is in India for a total period of one hundred and eighty-two days or more in that year, or is in India for sixty days or more during the year having been in India for three hundred and sixty-five days or more in the four preceding years.

Query: Is income from agriculture taxable?
Answer: Agricultural income is generally not included in total income for the purpose of computing tax, provided such income falls within the definition of agricultural income as specified in the Act.

Query: What constitutes salary income?
Answer: Income chargeable under the head 'Salaries' comprises wages, annuity or pension, gratuity, fees, commission, perquisites, profits in lieu of or in addition to salary, advances of salary, and payments received in respect of unavailed leave.

Query: Is there a standard deduction for salaried employees?
Answer: A standard deduction is allowable from salary income, limited to seventy-five thousand rupees or the amount of salary, whichever is less, where income-tax is computed under the new tax regime, or fifty thousand rupees in other cases.

Query: How is the value of a self-occupied house determined?
Answer: The annual value of a house property or part thereof is taken as nil if the owner occupies the property for their own residence or cannot occupy it owing to employment at another place, applicable to a maximum of two such houses.

Query: Can interest on a home loan be deducted?
Answer: A deduction is allowable for the amount of interest payable on capital borrowed for acquiring, constructing, repairing, renewing, or reconstructing the property, subject to a limit of two lakh rupees for self-occupied properties if acquisition or construction is completed within five years.

Query: What expenses are deductible for a business?
Answer: Deductions are allowable for rent, rates, taxes, repairs, and insurance for premises, machinery, plant, or furniture used wholly and exclusively for the purposes of the business or profession.

Query: Is a deduction allowed for bad debts?
Answer: A deduction is allowable for any amount of bad debt or part thereof which is written off as irrecoverable in the accounts of the assessee for the tax year, provided the debt has been taken into account in computing the income of the assessee for that or an earlier tax year.

Query: Is depreciation allowed on business assets?
Answer: A deduction is allowable for depreciation of tangible assets being buildings, machinery, plant, or furniture, and intangible assets being know-how, patents, copyrights, trademarks, licences, or franchises, owned and used for the purposes of the business or profession.

Query: Are large cash payments allowed for business expenses?
Answer: Expenditure for which payment or aggregate of payments made to a person in a day exceeds ten thousand rupees is not allowed as a deduction if such payment is not made through specified banking or online modes.

Query: Is there a presumptive tax scheme for small businesses?
Answer: Profits and gains of a specified business carried on by a resident individual, Hindu undivided family, or firm (excluding LLP) are deemed to be 8% (or 6% for digital receipts) of the total turnover if such turnover does not exceed two crore rupees (or three crore rupees in specified cases).

Query: What is included in the definition of a capital asset?
Answer: A 'capital asset' comprises property of any kind held by an assessee, whether connected with his business or not, and includes securities held by a Foreign Institutional Investor and Unit Linked Insurance Policies issued on or after 1st February, 2021.

Query: How are capital gains calculated?
Answer: Income chargeable under the head 'Capital gains' is computed by deducting from the full value of consideration received or accruing from the transfer of the capital asset the expenditure incurred wholly and exclusively in connection with such transfer and the cost of acquisition and improvement.

Query: Is tax exemption available when selling a house to buy another?
Answer: Capital gains arising from the transfer of a residential house are not charged to tax if the individual or Hindu undivided family purchases a new residential house within one year before or two years after the transfer, or constructs one within three years, subject to the cost of the new asset.

Query: Are lottery winnings taxable?
Answer: Winnings from lotteries, crossword puzzles, races, card games, and other games of any sort, or from gambling or betting, are chargeable to income-tax under the head 'Income from other sources'.

Query: Are gifts of money taxable?
Answer: Any sum of money received without consideration by a person is chargeable under 'Income from other sources' if the aggregate value exceeds fifty thousand rupees in a tax year, subject to exceptions for relatives and specific occasions.

Query: Is income from assets transferred to a spouse taxable?
Answer: Income arising directly or indirectly from assets transferred to a spouse without adequate consideration or not in connection with an agreement to live apart is included in the total income of the individual transferor.

Query: Can business losses be set off against salary?
Answer: A loss computed under the head 'Profits and gains of business or profession' cannot be set off against income chargeable under the head 'Salaries'.

Query: How long can business losses be carried forward?
Answer: Unabsorbed business loss (other than loss from speculation business) can be carried forward and set off against profits and gains of business or profession for up to eight tax years immediately succeeding the tax year in which the loss was first computed.

Query: Is a deduction allowed for life insurance premiums?
Answer: A deduction is allowable for the amount paid or deposited in the tax year for life insurance premia, deferred annuity, and contributions to provident funds, subject to an aggregate limit of one lakh fifty thousand rupees.

Query: Can health insurance premiums be deducted?
Answer: A deduction is allowable for health insurance premiums paid by any mode other than cash, generally up to twenty-five thousand rupees for the assessee and family, and an additional twenty-five thousand rupees for parents, with higher limits for senior citizens.

Query: Is interest on education loans deductible?
Answer: A deduction is allowable for the amount paid as interest on a loan taken from a financial institution or approved charitable institution for the purpose of pursuing higher education for the individual or a relative.

Query: Is there a tax benefit for electric vehicle loans?
Answer: A deduction is allowable for interest payable on a loan taken from a financial institution for the purchase of an electric vehicle sanctioned between 1st April 2019 and 31st March 2023, subject to a maximum of one lakh fifty thousand rupees.

Query: Are donations to charity deductible?
Answer: A deduction is allowable for sums paid as donations to certain funds and charitable institutions, limited to 50% or 100% of the donated sum depending on the fund, provided donations exceeding two thousand rupees are not made in cash.

Query: Can rent paid be deducted if HRA is not received?
Answer: A deduction is allowable for rent paid for residential accommodation by an assessee not receiving House Rent Allowance, to the extent such rent exceeds 10% of total income, subject to a maximum of five thousand rupees per month or 25% of total income.

Query: Is royalty income for authors deductible?
Answer: A deduction is allowable for resident individual authors deriving income from royalties or copyright fees for books of literary, artistic, or scientific nature, equal to the whole of such income or three lakh rupees, whichever is less.

Query: What deduction is available for persons with disability?
Answer: A deduction of seventy-five thousand rupees is allowable for a resident individual certified as a person with disability, and one lakh twenty-five thousand rupees for a person with severe disability.

Query: Is there a tax rebate for lower income?
Answer: A resident individual whose total income does not exceed five lakh rupees is entitled to a rebate of 100% of income-tax payable or twelve thousand five hundred rupees, whichever is less.

Query: What are the tax rates under the new regime?
Answer: The income-tax payable under the new tax regime for individuals is computed at rates ranging from nil for income up to four lakh rupees to 30% for income above twenty-four lakh rupees, with intermediate slabs taxed at 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, and 25%.

Query: Who must file a tax return?
Answer: Every person being a company or a firm, or any other person whose total income exceeds the maximum amount not chargeable to income-tax, is required to furnish a return of income within the prescribed time.

Query: Can a belated return be filed?
Answer: A person who has not furnished a return within the time allowed may furnish the return for any tax year at any time within nine months from the end of the relevant tax year or before the completion of the assessment, whichever is earlier.

Query: What is an updated return?
Answer: An updated return may be furnished by any person, whether or not a return has been previously furnished, within forty-eight months from the end of the financial year succeeding the relevant tax year, subject to payment of additional tax.

Query: Is quoting PAN mandatory?
Answer: Every person allotted a Permanent Account Number must quote such number in all returns, correspondence with income-tax authorities, and challans for payment of any sum due under the Act.

Query: When must advance tax be paid?
Answer: Liability for payment of advance tax arises during the tax year in respect of total income if the amount of tax payable during the year is ten thousand rupees or more.

Query: Is interest charged for late filing?
Answer: An assessee is liable to pay interest for default in furnishing the return of income if the return is not furnished by the due date or is not furnished.

Query: Can excess tax paid be refunded?
Answer: A refund is granted if the amount of tax paid by or on behalf of the assessee exceeds the amount with which the assessee is properly chargeable under the Act.

Query: What if tax is not deducted at source?
Answer: Any person who fails to deduct or pay the tax deductible at source is deemed to be an assessee in default and may be liable to pay interest and penalty.

Query: When is a tax audit required?
Answer: Every person carrying on business or profession is required to get accounts audited if the total sales, turnover, or gross receipts exceed specified limits, such as one crore rupees for business (or ten crore rupees for digital transactions) or fifty lakh rupees for profession.

Query: Can tax authorities search premises?
Answer: The competent authority may authorise a search and seizure operation if there is reason to believe that a person has failed to produce documents or is in possession of undisclosed income or property.

Query: What is a survey operation?
Answer: An income-tax authority may enter any place at which a business or profession is carried on to inspect books of account, verify cash or stock, and furnish information useful for any proceeding under the Act.

Query: Can an assessment order be appealed?
Answer: An assessee aggrieved by certain orders passed by an Assessing Officer may appeal to the Joint Commissioner (Appeals) or the Commissioner (Appeals) as per the appealable orders specified.

Query: What is Faceless Assessment?
Answer: Faceless Assessment is a scheme where assessment proceedings are conducted electronically to impart greater efficiency, transparency, and accountability by eliminating the interface between the income-tax authority and the assessee.

Query: How are crypto assets taxed?
Answer: Income from the transfer of any virtual digital asset is chargeable to tax at the rate of 30%, with no deduction allowed for any expenditure other than the cost of acquisition.

Query: What is the tax rate for online games?
Answer: Income by way of net winnings from any online game is chargeable to tax at the rate of 30%.

Query: How are lottery winnings taxed?
Answer: Winnings from lotteries, crossword puzzles, races, card games, and similar games are chargeable to tax at the rate of 30%.

Query: Is there a limit on cash loans?
Answer: No person shall take or accept from another person any loan or deposit or specified sum of twenty thousand rupees or more otherwise than by an account payee cheque, bank draft, or electronic clearing system.

Query: Is there a limit on receiving cash?
Answer: No person shall receive an amount of two lakh rupees or more in aggregate from a person in a day, or in respect of a single transaction, otherwise than by specified banking or electronic modes.

Query: What is the fee for late filing of return?
Answer: A person is liable to pay a fee for default in furnishing the return of income by the prescribed due date.

Query: Can mistakes in orders be rectified?
Answer: An income-tax authority may amend any order passed by it to rectify any mistake apparent from the record, within four years from the end of the financial year in which the order was passed.
